title: A Rooster, a Rent Bill and the 45-Minute Commute
title_zh: 一声鸡鸣、一张房租单与45分钟通勤
intro_zh: 本文约 535 词，CET-4 难度，含 6 个核心词（commute、afford、urban、rural、pace、isolation），句子复杂度中等，理解目标 85%-90%。文章通过两个人的清晨、一组调查数据和一个新出现的中间选择，讨论城市与乡村各自的价格与代价。

paragraphs.en: At 6:40 on a Monday, Li Wei stands pressed against the door of a subway car in Beijing, watching the stations slide past. Two hundred kilometres away, her cousin Zhang Min wakes to a rooster and the smell of wet grass. The two women are the same age and earn similar salaries. Their mornings, however, seem to belong to two different countries.
paragraphs.zh: 周一早上6点40分，李薇在北京挤在地铁车厢门边，看着一个个车站向后退去。两百公里外，她的表姐张敏在一声鸡鸣和湿草的气味中醒来。两个女人年纪相同，收入也差不多。然而她们的清晨，仿佛属于两个不同的国家。

paragraphs.en: Numbers help here. A 2024 survey of 2,000 workers found that people in big cities spend an average of 47 minutes commuting to work each way, and that rent swallows more than a third of many salaries. Few young workers can afford a flat within walking distance of the office, so the hours add up: nearly eight full days a year are spent underground. In a small town, the same flat may cost a tenth as much — but the survey also found that wages there are often 30 to 40 percent lower.
paragraphs.zh: 数字在这里能说明问题。2024年一项针对2000名职场人士的调查发现，大城市的人单程通勤平均要花47分钟，而房租吞掉了许多人三分之一以上的工资。很少有年轻上班族能负担得起步行可达办公室的房子，于是时间不断累加：一年有将近整整八天是在地下度过的。在小城镇，同样的房子可能只要十分之一的价钱——但同一项调查也发现，那里的工资往往低30%到40%。

paragraphs.en: The city sells something hard to measure: options. Within one subway stop you can reach a hospital that never closes, a library open until ten, an evening class in Japanese, and a shop that sells flour at midnight. For a young person this matters more than scenery. The city lets you try a job, leave it, and try another without moving house.
paragraphs.zh: 城市出售的是一种难以衡量的东西：选择。在地铁一站之内，你可以到达一家从不关门的医院、一家开到晚上十点的图书馆、一个日语夜校班，还有一家半夜也卖面粉的店。对年轻人来说，这比风景更重要。城市让你可以试一份工作、离开它、再试另一份，而不用搬家。

paragraphs.en: Yet the city charges for all of it, in money and in hours. Noise becomes background music you cannot switch off, and many people describe a tiredness that a long sleep does not fix. The urban rhythm is not simply fast; it is continuous. Bodies keep the score, as doctors like to say, and the bill often arrives at forty.
paragraphs.zh: 然而城市要为这一切收费，用钱，也用时间。噪音成了你关不掉的背景音乐，许多人描述一种睡再久也消不掉的疲惫。城市的节奏不只是快，而是不停。正如医生爱说的，身体会记账，而账单往往在四十岁时送到。

paragraphs.en: The rural world offers the opposite trade. A room of your own, a small garden, and neighbours who notice if your lights stay off for two days straight. Tomatoes in August cost almost nothing. Children ride bicycles on empty roads, and nobody needs to pay for a piano lesson to enjoy an afternoon. The pace here is set by weather rather than by a clock.
paragraphs.zh: 乡村世界提供的则是相反的交换。一间属于自己的房间、一个小菜园，还有会注意到你家灯连续两天没亮的邻居。八月的西红柿几乎不要钱。孩子们在空荡荡的路上骑自行车，没有人非得花钱上钢琴课才能享受一个下午。这里的节奏由天气决定，而不是由时钟决定。

paragraphs.en: The bill arrives in other forms. A serious illness may mean a ninety-minute drive to a proper hospital, and the ambulance may be a neighbour's car. Work is scarce. The internet, though far better than a decade ago, still fails in a storm. Young people often speak of isolation — the odd feeling of being the only person under thirty in the village.
paragraphs.zh: 账单会以别的形式到来。一场重病可能意味着开九十分钟车才能到一家像样的医院，而救护车也许是邻居的私家车。工作机会稀缺。网络虽然比十年前好得多，但一遇暴风雨仍然会断。年轻人常提到孤立感——那种村里唯一一个三十岁以下的人所感到的古怪滋味。

paragraphs.en: Remote work has cracked the old choice open. Some small towns now advertise cash payments to newcomers who bring their jobs with them. A couple in Zhejiang run a design studio from a town of 8,000 people and take the train to Shanghai once a month. Still, only some jobs can travel through a cable; a nurse, a cook or a bus driver cannot carry her work in a laptop.
paragraphs.zh: 远程办公把这个旧选择撬开了。一些小城镇如今公开承诺，凡是带着工作搬来的新居民可获现金补贴。浙江一对夫妇在一个人口八千的小镇上经营一家设计工作室，每月坐一次火车去上海。不过，只有部分工作能通过网线流动；护士、厨师或公交司机无法把工作装进笔记本电脑带走。

paragraphs.en: So the honest answer is duller than the argument. Neither place is better; each fits a different stage of life. The city suits people who need speed and choice. The countryside suits people who need space and quiet. Many families end up choosing both — a small flat in town, a family house in the village, and a train ticket between them that gets used more often than anyone expected.
paragraphs.zh: 所以诚实的答案比争论本身要平淡。两个地方都没有更好，各自适合不同的人生阶段。城市适合需要速度和选择的人，乡村适合需要空间和安静的人。许多家庭最终两个都要——城里一套小公寓、村里一栋老屋，以及一张往返其间、用得比谁都预想得更频繁的火车票。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The reasons why young people should move back to their home villages.
The trade-offs between city and country life, and how remote work is changing the choice.
Practical advice on how to save money on rent in big cities.
The history of housing prices in Chinese towns over the past decade.
questions.explain: 全文对比城市与乡村在通勤、房租、医疗、工作机会等方面的得与失，最后一层谈远程办公带来的新可能，因此B最全面。A、C、D都只是文中某个片段的放大或文中未涉及。

questions.q: According to the 2024 survey mentioned in the passage, which statement is true?
options: City workers spend an average of 47 minutes commuting to work each way.
Wages in small towns are usually 30 to 40 percent higher than in cities.
Rent in small towns is about a third of a worker's salary.
Most villagers now work from home with the help of the internet.
questions.explain: 细节题。第二段明确说单程通勤平均47分钟。B与原文相反（小城镇工资低30%-40%）；C混淆了“房租占工资三分之一”讲的是大城市；D文中无依据。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the couple in Zhejiang?
options: They gave up their city jobs completely and never go to Shanghai.
Their work requires them to be physically in Shanghai every day.
Their kind of work can be done at a distance, so they can enjoy both places.
They are planning to return to Shanghai within a year.
questions.explain: 推断题。文中说他们从人口八千的小镇经营设计工作室、每月去一次上海，可见其工作可远程完成，从而兼得两地好处。A“完全放弃”与每月去上海矛盾；B与远程办公相反；D文中未提。

questions.q: The sentence 'Bodies keep the score' in paragraph 4 most probably means that _______.
options: doctors write down their patients' weight at every visit
the effects of a fast, nonstop life show up in a person's health later on
people should count their steps carefully every day
sports records are more important than comfort
questions.explain: 词义题。该句出现在谈城市“用钱和时间收费”之后，接着一句是“账单往往在四十岁时送到”，说明长期快节奏、不间歇的生活会在健康上留下账目，即B。A、C、D均为字面误解。
